case.title: CATL, Ampace and Linergy Power
case.subtitle: Linergy Power Sdn Bhd · Serendah, Selangor, Malaysia
case.question: Can Sayari show how far up Linergy Power's ownership goes, whether it is part of the CATL group, and what it sends to US buyers?
case.answer: Partly. Sayari traces Linergy up to CATL and shows 17 rows of cells going to US buyers. But the percentages came from CATL's and TDK's filings, and Sayari missed the June 2026 sale that took Linergy out of the CATL group and into Japan's TDK.
case.why_it_matters: PFE tests look at who owns and controls the cell maker on the date of the transaction. Here the answer changed in June 2026: from a group CATL consolidates (CATL has been on the 1260H list since January 2025) to a Japanese company. Registry data that lags by months would give a buyer the wrong answer for later shipments. Earlier shipments would show the opposite problem if the registry were updated and no dates kept.
case.headline: Until June 2026 Linergy Power was 100% owned by Ampace's Hong Kong company, inside a Xiamen group that CATL consolidates with a 59.5% stake. TDK of Japan then bought all of it. Sayari still shows the old chain: 11 US-bound cell rows left under the CATL-group owner, and 6 to Eaton after the sale.
case.summary_for_non_experts: Linergy Power is a new battery-cell factory near Kuala Lumpur. It was set up in December 2024 by Ampace, a Chinese battery company that CATL, the world's biggest battery maker, controls together with ATL, a battery unit of Japan's TDK. Most of what the plant buys comes from China, much of it from Ampace itself. Its first cells went to US power-tool makers. In June 2026 TDK bought the whole plant, but the company records we searched hadn't been updated four months later.

steps.title: What Sayari's registry shows
steps.text: Malaysian company data names Ampace Technology Limited (Hong Kong) as Linergy's only shareholder. Above it, Sayari shows Xiamen Ampace, then Xiamen Xinnenghe, CATL and four Xiamen partnerships, then CATL's own shareholders. None of these links carries a percentage. One Linergy director, Jia Zhuocheng, has the same name as Xiamen Ampace's general manager.

steps.title: The percentages come from filings
steps.text: CATL's March 2026 filing calls Xiamen Ampace a consolidated subsidiary. Xinnenghe holds 85% of it, and CATL holds 59.5% indirectly. TDK's own releases put the joint venture behind Xinnenghe at 70% CATL and 30% ATL, TDK's battery unit. Until June 2026, then, Linergy sat inside a group that CATL controls. CATL has been on the US Section 1260H list since January 2025.

steps.title: In June 2026 the owner changed, and Sayari hasn't caught up
steps.text: On 19 May 2026 TDK said its Singapore unit, Amperex Technology (Singapore), would buy 100% of Linergy for US$241.1m, with the transfer set for 15 June. TDK's results for the quarter to 30 June confirm the purchase. On 18 October Sayari still showed Ampace as the shareholder, and showed no Linergy under the Singapore company. A buyer screening Linergy in registry data would still see a CATL-group owner.

steps.title: Chinese materials in, much of it from the parent
steps.text: Of 2,759 inbound rows (May 2025 to Jun 2026), 2,679 left from China. Xiamen Ampace itself sent 1,044, including cathode and anode material, carbon black and copper and aluminium foil. Graphite came from Zhongke Shinzoom (14 rows) and Shanshan (3), cathode powder (HS 2842.90) from XTC, Qinghai Taifeng Pulead and Chengdu B&M, and electrolyte from Tinci, Capchem and a forwarder. Much of the rest is production-line equipment.

steps.title: Cells out to the US, before and after the sale
steps.text: 17 rows of cells and battery systems (HS 8507, rechargeable batteries) went to the US. Before the sale, Nov 2025 to Feb 2026: 11 rows of 18650 and 21700 power-tool cells, to Ampace's own Hong Kong company (6), Milwaukee Tool (3), Stanley Black & Decker (1) and Techtronic (1). After the sale, Aug to Sep 2026: 6 rows of battery systems to Eaton in Raleigh, North Carolina. No rows show for Mar to Jul 2026, because the Malaysian export data stops in February.

steps.title: Buyers' own records don't link to Ampace or CATL
steps.text: We asked Sayari for the shortest path from Eaton to CATL and from Milwaukee Tool to Xiamen Ampace. Both run only through trade: buyer, then Linergy, then Ampace's Hong Kong company. Neither buyer has an ownership or officer link to the group. Their exposure is through what they buy, and that depends on the date of each shipment.

detected.text: Registry chain: Linergy ← Ampace Technology (HK) ← Xiamen Ampace ← Xinnenghe and CATL, with CATL's own shareholders above.
From filings, not Sayari: Ampace (HK) held 100% of Linergy until June 2026; Xinnenghe holds 85% of Xiamen Ampace; CATL holds 59.5% indirectly and consolidates it.
TDK bought 100% of Linergy through Amperex Technology (Singapore): agreed 19 May 2026, transfer set for 15 June, confirmed in TDK's results for the quarter to 30 June.
Sayari still showed the pre-sale owner on 18 Oct 2026, and no Linergy under the Singapore buyer.
17 artificial-graphite rows from Zhongke Shinzoom and Shanshan, plus cathode powder, electrolyte, foils and anode materials, almost all from China and much from the parent.
17 US-bound rows: 11 before the sale (Ampace HK, Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, Techtronic), 6 after it (Eaton).
CATL has been on the Section 1260H list since the 6 January 2025 update.

suggested.text: CATL's look-through stake in Linergy before the sale was about 59.5%, assuming Xiamen Ampace owns all of Ampace (HK). Sayari gives no percentage for that link.
The Linergy director Jia Zhuocheng is probably Xiamen Ampace's general manager 贾琢成 (name only).
HS 2842.90 rows from XTC, Pulead and Chengdu B&M are cathode powder; the code and supplier names fit, but most rows carry no product text.

not_visible.text: Any shipments from Mar to Jul 2026, and anything Linergy received after the sale: the Malaysian trade data ends in February 2026.
Whether Linergy still buys from Xiamen Ampace and other CATL-group suppliers under TDK ownership.
Which graphite went into which cells, and whether the Eaton battery systems contain cells made before the sale.
Whether any of these buyers claims a US tax credit, and how the PFE rules would treat each shipment.

red_flags.flag: Chinese parent ownership of the transit plant
red_flags.note: Until June 2026: 100% Ampace (HK), in a group CATL consolidates (59.5%). Since then: TDK (Japan) 100%, per TDK's filings.

red_flags.note: Registered 19 Dec 2024; first inbound row May 2025; first US row 18 Nov 2025. Normal for a new plant.

red_flags.flag: Volume spike after a policy date
red_flags.note: CATL's January 2025 listing predates the plant. The Eaton rows begin after the TDK sale, but the Mar–Jul 2026 data gap hides any trend.

red_flags.flag: Shared address or officer with a flagged entity
red_flags.note: A Linergy director shares the name of Xiamen Ampace's general manager; Xiamen Ampace is owned by a 1260H-listed company. Name match only.
Xiamen Ampace has a registry record and separate trade records; Eaton and Milwaukee Tool have two records each; Linergy's name appears as 'Linery'.
ASPI and Sheffield Hallam sub-tier flags on the plant via its suppliers. Context, not a finding.

caveats: Making cells in Malaysia from Chinese materials is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
Buyers are named because they appear in customs records. That says nothing about their compliance, or whether they claim any US tax credit.
The ownership percentages come from CATL's and TDK's filings and from The Edge's reading of the Malaysian registry, not from Sayari.
CATL's 59.5% applies to Xiamen Ampace. Carrying it down to Linergy assumes Xiamen Ampace owns all of Ampace (HK); Sayari shows the link without a percentage.
Sayari lists CATL as a direct shareholder of Xiamen Ampace too. CATL's filing describes only the indirect stake, so that record may be out of date.
TDK set the share transfer for 15 June 2026 and reported completion within the quarter to 30 June. We use mid-June as the change date; the exact day isn't confirmed.
Before the sale TDK already held 25.5% of Linergy indirectly, through ATL's stake in the joint venture. Japanese and Chinese interests were mixed from the start.
No trade rows show for Mar–Jul 2026. The Malaysian export source ends in February 2026, and the US import rows for Linergy start in August.
The Eaton rows list Tawau, in Sabah, as the departure port, far from the Selangor plant. Treat route details with care.
The 1260H date comes from law-firm and trade-press summaries of the DoD list; we didn't open the Federal Register notice.
Records checked on 18 Oct 2026. Sayari may add the TDK link later.

TDK of Japan bought 100% through Amperex Technology (Singapore) in June 2026. Sayari still shows the Ampace chain. 2,759 inbound rows (2,679 from China); 17 US-bound rows of cells and battery systems, Nov 2025 to Sep 2026.

calls.result_summary: CATL's guarantee-quota announcements (cninfo, 10 Mar 2026 and 15 Mar 2025) list Xiamen Ampace as a consolidated controlled subsidiary: Xiamen Xinnenghe holds 85%, CATL holds 59.5% indirectly; legal representative 贾琢成; registered capital RMB 5bn; 2025 revenue about RMB 12.6bn. Also returned CATL's Q1 2026 report (top shareholder 厦门瑞庭投资 22.45%) and a 2024 article describing Xinnenghe as 70% CATL, 30% ATL-owned 新能同.
calls.interpretation: CATL consolidates Xiamen Ampace and holds 59.5% of it, so until June 2026 Linergy sat inside the CATL group.

calls.question: What do TDK's disclosures say about the CATL–ATL joint ventures?
calls.result_summary: TDK releases (28 Apr 2021, 27 Apr 2022): the cell joint venture (RMB 5bn) is ATL 30%, CATL 70%; the pack joint venture is ATL 70%, CATL 30%; a new Xiamen holding company (representative Jia Zhuocheng) is 100% ATL. calls.interpretation: Confirms the 70% CATL stake in the 85% holder. ATL is a TDK subsidiary, so TDK had an indirect stake all along.

params.query: Linergy Power acquisition shares Ampace Technology Amperex Technology Singapore

calls.question: Did TDK buy Linergy, and from whom?
calls.result_summary: TDK release, 19 May 2026: Amperex Technology (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. to acquire 100% (1,017,605,244 shares) of Linergy for US$240m plus US$1.1m fees; board resolution and agreement 19 May 2026; share transfer scheduled 15 Jun 2026; Linergy net assets US$217.3m at 31 Mar 2026. The Edge, 20 May 2026: per the Companies Commission of Malaysia, Linergy is wholly owned by Ampace Technology Ltd; TDK withheld the seller's name at the major shareholder's request.
calls.interpretation: Confirms the pre-sale 100% Ampace stake and the planned date of the change of owner.

params.query: TDK first quarter fiscal 2026 results Linergy Power acquired all shares consolidated subsidiary

calls.question: Did the sale complete?
calls.result_summary: TDK's results for the three months to 30 Jun 2026 (filed 31 Jul 2026) say TDK Group acquired all shares of Linergy Power in the quarter. The 19 May release adds that TDK already held 25.5% indirectly and had no personnel link.
calls.interpretation: Linergy has been a TDK subsidiary since about mid-June 2026. The 25.5% fits ATL's 30% of the 85% holder (our arithmetic).
